(1) ExactBSD = Exact-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-Formula-from-Low-Selmer-Corank-October-7-2026/build/sections/. Standing hypothesis of Section 5, 05-single.tex:3-10, verbatim: 'Fix an odd prime \(p\). In this section \(E/\Q\) is non-CM and has analytic rank zero or one. The purpose is to prove \(X(E)\geq0\), where \(X(E)=v_p(Q_E)-v_p\bigl(\#\Sha(E/\Q)\bigr)\). The rank and finiteness conclusions of Theorem~\ref{classical:analytic-low-rank} are in force.' The determinant setup, 05-single.tex:360-380: 'Take the rational auxiliary tuple of Section~\ref{sec:vertical}, with one tame variable for each moving prime and a genuine cyclotomic variable \(t\). Put \(R=\Z_p[[t,u_1,\ldots,u_k]]\), \(M_R=T\otimes_{\Z_p}R(\chi)\). ... The complex \(G\) is the limiting unrestricted global complex, with the moving primes allowed in its support. ... Let \(z\in H^1(G)\) be the smoothed square class with symbol evaluation one and degeneracy \(A=1\).' Proposition 5.5 (single:integral), 05-single.tex:404-414, verbatim: 'The generic cohomology of \(G\) is a line in degree one, and \(z\) is nonzero on that line. If \(U_0\in\Frac R\) is its coordinate in the inverse determinant relative to an integral generator, then \(U=\frac{U_0}{\Delta}\prod_{q\in S_f\setminus\{p\}}\frac{D_q}{P_q}\ \in R\setminus\{0\}\). (3)' with \(D_q=\det(1-\chi(\Frob_q)\rho_T(\Frob_q)/q\mid V_{I_q})\) (05-single.tex:382-386) and the note 05-single.tex:390-394: 'The polynomials are respectively quadratic at good reduction, signed linear at multiplicative reduction, and one at additive reduction. Thus they are integral, including when \(p\) divides a Tamagawa number.' Its proof (05-single.tex:416-424 and 630-760) states: 'At \((p)\), \eqref{eq:source-1}(a) identifies \(G\) with a free line in degree one' (eq. (1)(a) = Proposition 4.2 (vertical:tests), 04-vertical.tex:173-183: '(a) \(G\otimes_RR_{(p)}\) is a free line in degree one'); generic nonvanishing from 'Rohrlich's finite-support twist nonvanishing, in the form \cite[Theorem 13.5(2)]{Kato}'; horizontal divisors by Lemma 5.6 (single:line, 05-single.tex:445-459: 'suppose that the chosen square or rectangular system class \(z_{\rm sys}\) is generically nonzero. Then the global complex has a single generic cohomology line in degree one. At each of the indicated DVRs, \(d(G_{\rm test},z_{\rm sys})\geq0\). (4)'), whose proof uses 'Global invariants vanish by the non-CM open-image argument \cite{Serre}', Chebotarev-chosen derivative primes, Lemma 3.x (models:line-switch, 03-models.tex:339-365), and 'one fixed nonzero \(p\)-power \(L_*\) which clears all torsion ambiguities'; removal of the fixed factors by Lemma models:poles with the explicit disclaimer 05-single.tex:720-722: 'There is no assertion of a uniform denominator for these stage quotients.' Section 4 setup, 04-vertical.tex:12-16, verbatim: 'Use the fields \(K,F,L\) and discriminants \(D,D'\) of Section~\ref{sec:classical}. In particular \(p\) splits completely in \(L\), the residual division field is disjoint from \(L\), and both \(E/K\) and \(E^{D'}/K\) have rank one and finite Tate--Shafarevich group.' Lemma 2.6 (classical:auxiliary-fields), 02-classical.tex:115-140: 'Let \(E/\Q\) have conductor \(N\) and analytic rank \(r\in\{0,1\}\). There exist coprime negative odd fundamental discriminants \(D,D'<-4\) such that ... (i) Every prime dividing \(2Np\) splits in both imaginary quadratic fields ... (ii) The analytic ranks of \(E^D,E^{D'},E^{DD'}\) are respectively \(1-r,1-r,r\).' (proved from Theorem 2.5 = '\cite[Theorem~1.2]{Goldfeld}', 02-classical.tex:104-113).

(2) ExactBSD Proposition 5.11 (single:center), 05-single.tex:1276-1284, verbatim: 'The element \(U\) of Proposition~\ref{single:integral} satisfies \(X(E)=v_p(U(0))\ge0\). (8) This holds at every odd coefficient prime, for all reduction types and all residual representations of the non-CM curve.' Proof 05-single.tex:1286-1379: integral Poitou-Tate (single:pt) in rank zero and rank one ('In rank one, let \(P\) generate the full free Mordell--Weil group modulo torsion' and 'The logarithm is nonzero by \eqref{eq:source-5}' = Prop 5.7, which assumes \(\ord_{s=1}L(E,s)=1\)), Lemma 3.9 (models:haar) Haar identities \(\tau_q=v_p(c_qP_q(1))\), and the limit step 'determinant pivots of the same ranks survive the limit by Remark~\ref{models:central-pivots}. The raw valuation is unchanged.'

(3) ExactBSD Section 6 standing setup, 06-pair.tex:3-9, verbatim: 'Fix an odd prime \(p\). We retain the imaginary quadratic field \(K\), the auxiliary field \(L\), and the tuple of tame directions constructed in Sections~\ref{sec:classical} and~\ref{sec:vertical}. Thus \(p=w\bar w\) in \(K\), every rational prime below the fixed finite support for \(E/K\) splits in \(K\)'. Proposition 6.1 (pair:primitive), 06-pair.tex:84-106: 'On the canonical ordinary locus define \(f^{[p]}=(1-a_pV_p+p\epsilon_pV_p^2)f\), \(F_0=\lim_{j\to\infty}d_{\rm mod}^{(p-1)p^j-1}f^{[p]}\), \(F=\prod_{q\in S^\circ}P_q(V_q)F_0\). The limits are integral weight-zero functions. ... the expansion \(F(z)\) is the transform of a bounded integral measure \(\mu\) on \(\Z_p\), supported on \(\Z_p^\times\). On every interior CM disk one has the exact identity \(F_0=P_p(V_p)G\). (9)', preceded (06-pair.tex:76-82) by 'We give the argument at odd \(p\), including the case \(p\mid N\). Here \emph{ordinary} refers to the elliptic curves parametrized by the modular source. It imposes no ordinary-reduction hypothesis on the target \(E\)'. Proposition 6.5 (pair:vertical-primitivity), 06-pair.tex:406-413: 'For each of the tuples under consideration and either \(p\)-adic place, \(p\nmid B_w\). (14)' (proof 06-pair.tex:415-610 via '\cite[Proposition~3.11 and Corollary~3.13]{HidaMu}', '\cite[Sections~2 and~5]{ChaiOrd}' and '\cite[Proposition~5.3]{ChaiOrd}', Zarhin, Chebotarev). Corollary 6.9 (pair:integral-quotient), 06-pair.tex:1048-1058: 'Using the descended analytic ideals, the fraction \(U_w=B_w/L_w\) is represented by an integral series, and \(p\nmid U_w\).' Theorem 9.6 (unit:unit-comparison), 09-unit.tex:396-401: 'The two quotients \(U_w\) are units. Their specialization with all artificial variables zero gives an integral unit comparison between the analytic series and strict determinant on the true anticyclotomic line.' Section 9 opening, 09-unit.tex:3-5: 'Fix the odd prime \(p\) and the auxiliary fields of Lemma~\ref{classical:auxiliary-fields}.' Here \(L_w\) is 'the determinant of the strict-at-\(w\), full-at-\(\bar w\) complex' for \(E/K\) with \(K\) the auxiliary field of Lemma 2.6 (so rank \(E(K)=1\), 04-vertical.tex:15-16).

(4) TwoPrimary = The-two-primary-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-formula-in-Selmer-corank-at-most-one-October-6-2026/build/sections/. 05-positive-determinant.tex:5-10: 'The central specialization is computed here in analytic rank zero; Section~\ref{sec:positive-completion} treats rank one and a center of initially unknown analytic rank. Throughout the construction itself, no analytic-rank hypothesis is imposed.' Proposition 5.1 (prop:positive-determinant:integral), 05-positive-determinant.tex:34-61: 'The complex \(C^+\otimes_B B_{(2)}\) is a free module of rank two in degree one, up to homotopy. Generically over \(B\), the tensor \(a\wedge z\) is nonzero and gives a coordinate \(U_{\rm raw}\in\operatorname{Frac}B\) ... \(U=\frac{U_{\rm raw}}{\Delta}\prod_{q\in S_f, q\ne2}\frac{D_q}{P_q}\) (L1) ... The assertion is that \(U\in B\setminus\{0\}\).' (for 'the non-CM curve \(E'\)', :14; \(B=\mathbb Z_2[[t,u_1,\ldots,u_k]]\)). Lemma 5.7 (lem:positive-determinant:rank-zero), 05-positive-determinant.tex:501-512: 'For either branch \(A_0\) of the construction, if \(\mathrm{an}(A_0)=0\), then the normalized determinant satisfies \(v_2 U(0)=X(A_0)\). (L5) In particular \(X(A_0)\ge0\). If only \(s_2(A_0)=0\) is known and \(U\) is a unit, then \(L(A_0,1)\ne0\), and hence \(X(A_0)=0\).' Lemma 7.5 (lem:positive-completion:bockstein), 07-positive-completion.tex:237-242: 'For the direction of Lemma~\ref{lem:positive-completion:direction}, \(\operatorname{ord}_v\delta(v)=1\). In particular, \(C_f^{\rm Sel}\) is generically acyclic over \(\mathcal R\).' Standing: 07-positive-completion.tex:3-4 'All curves in this section are non-CM', :9-10 'For an initially unknown center of Selmer corank one', :225-227 'the degree-one dimension is \(s_2=1\)'.

(5) Goldfeld2 = Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-October-7-2026/build/sections/. Lemma (lem:cy:residual-free), 04-cyclotomic.tex:580-586, verbatim: 'If \(E[2]\) is an extension of two trivial \(\F_2\)-modules, then there is an isomorphism in the derived category \(C_S^+(\mathbb T)\otimes_R\mathcal O[G]\simeq \mathcal O[G]^2[-1]\).' (\(R=\Lambda[G]\), \(\Lambda=\Z_2[[t]]\) the real cyclotomic \(\Z_2\)-extension, 04-cyclotomic.tex:34-58). Proof cites '\cite[Proposition~3.2.11 and Remark~3.2.12]{SharifiIwasawa}' and 'Ferrero--Washington gives \(\mu(X)=0\)'. It serves Theorem (thm:cyclotomic-bound), 01-arithmetic-transfer.tex:250-259: 'Suppose that \(E[2]\) is an extension of two trivial \(\F_2\)-modules. There is a constant \(C_E\) such that every odd fundamental discriminant \(h\) prime to \(2N\) with \(L(E^{(h)},1)\ne0\) satisfies \(v(\mathcal L(h))\ge 2w(h)+s(h)-C_E\).'

(6) SelmerConverse = The-Selmer-converse-for-elliptic-curves-at-every-prime-October-7-2026/build/sections/. Main theorem 01-*.tex:25-37: 'For every elliptic curve \(A_0/\Q\), every prime \(p\), and \(r\in\{0,1\}\), \(s_p(A_0)=r \Longrightarrow a(A_0)=\rank_{\Z}A_0(\Q)=r, \#\Sha(A_0/\Q)<\infty\).' Section 3 standing, 03-tame-deformation.tex:3-6: 'We retain the fields and the contradiction assumption of \cref{sec:reduction}. In particular, the conductor-one Heegner trace \(y\in A_0(K)\) is torsion.' and :30-31 'The two places \(v,v^c\) of \(K\) above \(p\) have completion \(\Q_p\)' (p split in K). Equation (5.katz-abelian-log), 05-constant-terms.tex:318-322: '\(F_0(x)=\kappa^{-1}\sum_r e_rp^{-r}\log_{A_0,p}\bigl(\varphi(\mathrm{Fr}^{r}x)\bigr)\)', with :335-337 'No ordinary hypothesis on \(A_0\) at \(p\) has entered this argument.' and :218-227 'Their construction [BDP 2013, Prop 3.24] is made under \(p\nmid N\). We give the primitive and logarithm comparison for the reduction types occurring here.' Lemma 3.6 (lem:uniform-local-log), 03-tame-deformation.tex:697-711: 'Fix an integer \(d_0\ge0\). There is a constant \(c\) such that, for every finite unramified extension \(E/\Q_p\) with \(v_p([E:\Q_p])\le d_0\), \(\log_{A_0,p}(A_0(E))\subseteq p^{-c}\cO_E\). If \(P\in A_0(E)\) and the Kummer class of \(p^C P\) vanishes in \(H^1(E,A_0[p^n])\), where \(C,n\ge0\) are integers, then \(v_p(\log_{A_0,p}P)\ge n-C-c\).'
